## In one sentence

Linear algebra studies vectors, matrices, and the transformations that connect
them.

## Vectors and matrices

A vector can represent measurements, coordinates, or a direction. A matrix
stores numbers in rows and columns and can represent a linear transformation or
a dataset. Matrix multiplication combines transformations and is not generally
commutative: $AB$ may differ from $BA$.

The dot product measures alignment:

$$
\mathbf{x} \cdot \mathbf{y} = \sum_{i=1}^{p} x_i y_i
$$

Orthogonal vectors have dot product zero. Length and angle are often the most
useful geometric interpretations.

## Linear systems

A system $A\mathbf{x}=\mathbf{b}$ asks which vector is mapped to $\mathbf{b}$.
Row reduction reveals whether solutions are unique, multiple, or impossible.
The columns of $A$ determine the space of possible outputs.

## Eigenvalues and applications

An eigenvector keeps its direction under a transformation:
$A\mathbf{v}=\lambda\mathbf{v}$. Eigenvalues help describe repeated processes,
principal components, and long-run behaviour.

::: {.callout-tip}
Check dimensions before multiplying matrices. If $A$ is $m \times n$, then the
next matrix must have $n$ rows.
:::

## Check your understanding

Represent three observations with two measurements as a matrix. Identify its
rows, columns, and the meaning of a matrix-vector product.
